name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets have leaned on AI-linked mega-cap tech [the very largest companies by value], so doubts about AI spending hit the whole index. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12 and an AI selloff followed. Since then, official papers have warned that AI valuations are stretched and increasingly debt-funded.
today: Headlines say Anthropic's stock surged in its Thursday debut, yet the market dove anyway. One says investors sold other AI stocks to buy into it. Another says Alphabet fell as the debut put a fresh value on Google's stake. Earlier debriefs said the Nasdaq rose 0.42% on an earlier day, so AI was not a one-way selloff then. Today it clearly was, with the Nasdaq down 2.25%. Asia's Friday reaction, outside today's close, was ugly: SoftBank fell over 16% and the Nikkei [Japan's main stock index] fell 2.9%. Chip names also faced China headlines, which are covered below. A headline says the S&P 500 has now fallen four straight weeks from a record high.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up headline inflation [the total price rise, including food and energy]. Central banks must decide whether that fades or leaks into wages and services, and after 2021 they are less willing to wait. The euro area hit 4% inflation, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
today: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson spoke on how to handle shocks. He said an energy price shock raises inflation while hurting incomes, so there is a tradeoff. He said a stronger response is warranted if inflation expectations risk becoming unanchored. Governor Barr said yesterday that inflation is too high and further hikes will likely be appropriate. The Fed minutes were released Wednesday, but only a notice was provided, so their details are unknown. Bailey said UK inflation, at 3.6% in October, should reach about 5% by mid-next year, but he sees limited knock-on effects so far. The BOJ chief signaled a near-term hike, and Japan's core inflation hit its highest this year as an energy subsidy expired.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout. Markets ask how divided government would change tariffs, spending and the dollar. Earlier debriefs said the dollar had its biggest rally since 2024, and that Barclays and Deutsche Bank think the AI boom could extend dollar strength.
today: The dollar index rose 0.05% to 103.91, and a WSJ headline says it hit a new 52-week high. Another headline says the dollar extended its rally as risk appetite fades. No headline ties today's move to the election. It looks tied to fear and Fed hike talk, though that is an inference. Gold fell 4.48%, and a headline blames elevated yields and a strong dollar.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the currency market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The BOJ's 1.25% rate is 2.625 percentage points below the Fed's 3.875%, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars. Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.
today: USD/JPY was 159.32, down 0.04%, so the yen was little changed. The BOJ chief played down soft consumption data and signaled a near-term rate hike. Japan's inflation accelerated, and the country posted a sixth straight monthly trade deficit. A Reuters-style analysis says BOJ ambiguity on the path of hikes could tempt yen bears. In Friday's Asian session, the Nikkei fell 2.9% on chip and metals stocks.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict that began in early 2026 cut global oil output by 12 mb/d [million barrels per day] in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because the world was oversupplied and stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned.
today: WTI fell 3.85% to 82.7 dollars as headlines pointed to supply-surplus expectations. Energy stocks slid, and Canada's TSX fell 2.1% on weak metals and energy. Yet the war still pushes energy costs up elsewhere. The ECB's Vujčić says it lifts European energy prices, the UK has record diesel prices, and Bailey says the conflict is in its ninth month.
